citation: Habek M, Ruška B, Crnošija L, Adamec I, Junaković A, Krbot Skorić M. Effect of Food Intake on Hemodynamic Parameters during the Tilt-Table Test in Patients with Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome. J Clin Neurol. 2019;15(2):205-210.
protocol: Tilt-table protocol: 10 min supine, 10 min at 70 degrees, then 400 mL Nutridrink Multi Fibre liquid meal (per 100 mL: 5.8 g fat, 6 g protein, 18 g carbohydrate; 300 kcal per 200 mL), then 45 min supine and 10 min tilted; HR and BP before and after the meal.
population: POTS group n=41 (29 female; age 29.74 +/- 10.61 y), split by heart-rate response to the meal: A n=13, B n=12, C n=16. Healthy group D n=10 (6 female; age 24.25 +/- 2.25 y).

reports.marker: systolic BP (supine rows, before and after meal)
diastolic BP (supine rows, before and after meal)
heart rate (supine rows, before and after meal)

note: Healthy group D (n=10) is printed separately in Table 1 with pre- and post-meal values (mean +/- SD). Use the supine rows only: the tilted rows are posture-specific and the model has no posture input. Grams are per 100 mL, so 400 mL is derivable but not printed. The post-meal value is a single supine window, not a stated minute.
